_meta.purpose: Tags that make the items of references.json retrievable by environment and by information need. An entry points to one reference item (or one row of it) and says which needs it is about, what kind of statement it is, and which conditions the item itself states. pipeline/findings.py checks the tags against references.json and writes data/pipeline/findings.csv and data/pipeline/findings_by_environment.json. The layer adds tags only: the text and the quote of an item are carried unchanged, and no value of this file enters the counts, tiers or indicators of the pipeline.
_meta.tagging: Every tag (needs, kind, conditions, the choice of the words given as basis, and the choice of which items are included) was made by an AI reading of the items of references.json on 2026-11-14. It was not checked by a human. The documents themselves were not opened again for this file: a tag rests on the item as written in references.json.

rules.stated_only: A condition (oxygen, pressure, gravity level, flow, fuel phase, material) is attached to an entry only if the item states it in its own 'text', 'quote' or 'values', as a number or as an explicit word. The item's 'note', its 'where' and the title of the document are not used. A condition the item does not state is absent from the entry; absent does not mean any.
rules.whole_statement: A condition is normalized only if it is a condition of the whole statement of the entry. A condition written for one part of an item (for one of several limits, for one side of a comparison) is kept as words under 'condition_words' and is not normalized, unless the item is split into rows.
rules.words_only: Where the item names a condition without a value that can be compared ('elevated oxygen', 'reduced pressure', 'low gravity', 'reduced gravity', 'quiescent'), the words are copied under 'condition_words' and the normalized field stays empty. No number is supplied for such words.
rules.results_are_not_conditions: An oxygen number that is the reported result (a limiting oxygen concentration, LOI, ULOI, MOC, a flammability boundary, a difference between limits) is not the atmosphere of a test and is not normalized as 'o2_pct'. It stays in the item's text and values. Such an entry is matched on the pressure and the gravity level the item states for the limit.
rules.gravity: A gravity level is normalized only from an explicit word of 'gravity_vocabulary'. 'low gravity', 'low-g' and 'reduced gravity' are kept as words, because the documents use them for microgravity, for partial gravity or for both. If an item names a gravity condition in such words next to a level that can be normalized, no level is normalized, so that the entry is not tied to a part of what the item says. An item that reports results at several levels (a comparison) carries the list of the levels.
rules.rows: An item that states several condition sets becomes one entry for each set, and 'row' names it: one entry for each row of 'values.rows' ('row_source' points to the row), one for each pressure of a list of pressures or each pressure column of a table, and, for two items without rows in 'values' (SAF45.table2, H2011.cannot), one for each condition set written in the text. Every entry of an item carries the whole text and quote of the item.
rules.pressure: Pressure is normalized to kPa with fixed factors: 1 psi = 6.894757 kPa, 1 atm = 101.325 kPa; kPa is kept. The result is rounded to 3 decimals. 'pressure_as_written' holds the item's own words with the unit. Where the item writes a pressure in kPa and repeats it in psia, the kPa number is used. '1 atm' and '1 atmosphere' are normalized to 101.325 kPa although the documents use them as a nominal statement.
rules.oxygen: Oxygen is normalized as the percentage written in the item, without conversion and without a statement of basis (the items write %, mol %, % by volume). A cell with two numbers ('21.7 to 21.5') is a range [min, max]; '> 30%' is an open range.
rules.unchanged: No statement is reworded. The outputs carry 'text', 'quote' and 'where' of the item exactly as in references.json, and the access level of the document. An item from a document whose 'access' is not 'full_text_read' is carried with that access level in every output.
rules.included: Included: every item of type published_result, knowledge_gap and limitation, except those listed under 'left_out' with the reason; and those items of type design_value, definition, requirement, acceptance_criterion and recommendation that state how fire or smoke behaves, what a test or a standard requires in a condition, or what a quantity used for such a statement means. Not included: items of type stated_objective and framework; items of type operational_practice, monitoring_range and exposure_limit; design values that only name an atmosphere or a flow range (they are the basis of the scenarios); definitions and requirements that describe an apparatus, a procedure, a data column or the hardware settings of an experiment.
rules.needs: 'needs' is decided from the words of the item: P1 limiting oxygen, flammability limit or threshold, flammability of materials, Test 1; P2 ignition; P3 flame spread, fire growth, burn length; S1 extinction, extinguishing agents and suppressants, suppression; D1 combustion products and gases; D2 smoke particles and smoke detectors. 'fire signatures' is tagged D1 and D2. An item about fire safety as a whole, about detection or fire protection without naming gases or smoke, or one that only states test conditions, is tagged 'general'. The tags differ in places from the 'references' lists of needs.json, which were made for another purpose.
rules.kind: result = something observed, measured or concluded and reported by a document, including the conditions under which tests were run; criterion = what a standard or a document requires or defines (a test condition, a pass criterion, the meaning of a quantity); gap = something a document says is not known, not available or still to be determined; caveat = a limit on using a result. Items of type knowledge_gap are tagged gap and items of type limitation are tagged caveat. An entry has one kind; where an item holds more than one, 'unsure' says so.

fields.item: id of the item in references.json
fields.row: name of the condition set, for an item split into several entries
fields.row_source: path in the item's 'values' of the row the entry was made from
fields.column_of / column_index: for an entry made from one column of a table stored as lists: the 'values' key of the table and the index of the column
fields.needs: subset of P1, P2, P3, S1, D1, D2, or ['general']
fields.conditions: only the stated ones. o2_pct: a value or [min, max] (null for an open end; 'o2_pct_exclusive' names an end that is not included), with o2_as_written; pressure_kpa: a value or [min, max], with pressure_as_written; gravity_level: list of microgravity, lunar, martian, normal, partial; flow_cms: a value, with flow_as_written; fuel_phase: solid, liquid or gas; material: list of names as written
fields.condition_basis: for each normalized condition, where the item states it: {'in': 'text' or 'quote', 'words': exact words} or {'in': 'values', 'key': path}; a gravity basis also names its 'level'
fields.condition_words: conditions the item names in words that cannot be compared; exact words of the item's text or quote
fields.unsure: what the tagger was not sure about, or a choice made in the tagging; written by the AI, not a sentence of the document

lists.compared: For each scenario of scenarios.json and each need (and for the entries tagged 'general'), every entry is compared with the scenario on oxygen, pressure and gravity level. Oxygen and pressure use the scenario's ranges with their inclusive flags (a minimum is included and a maximum is not, unless the scenario says otherwise). A stated value is 'inside' or 'outside'. A stated range is 'inside' if both of its ends are inside, 'outside' if no part of it is, and 'overlaps' otherwise; an open range can only overlap or be outside. Gravity is 'same' if one of the levels the entry states is the level of the scenario, or if the entry states partial gravity and the scenario is lunar or Martian (recorded as 'finding_states_partial_gravity'); otherwise it is 'different'. A condition the entry does not state is 'not_stated'; one the scenario does not set is 'not_set'.
lists.at_environment: The entry states an oxygen and a pressure and both are inside the scenario's ranges. If the scenario sets a gravity level and the entry states a different one, the entry is not listed: it is counted under other_conditions and recorded under 'moved_for_gravity' with the reason. An entry that states no gravity level stays in this list and carries gravity_level under 'not_stated'.
lists.about_a_stated_condition_of_the_environm: The entry is not at_environment; at least one of its oxygen, pressure and gravity level is inside (or the same as) the scenario's, or its stated range overlaps the scenario's range; and none of the three is outside or different. An overlap counts for this list only and is marked 'overlaps'.
lists.general: The entry has no normalized oxygen, pressure or gravity level: criteria, gaps and caveats that apply as written. An entry of this list that names a condition in words carries 'states_conditions_in_words': true; read the words before using it for an environment.
lists.other_conditions: Everything else: an entry with a condition outside the scenario's ranges or a different gravity level, and an entry that states only conditions the scenario does not set. These entries are counted and not listed.
lists.matched_on: For each listed entry: the conditions that matched, with the entry's own value and its words, and the relation. 'not_stated' names the scenario's conditions that the entry does not state. Where the scenario sets a flow range, 'flow' gives the relation of the entry's flow; it does not change the list.
lists.general_need: Entries tagged 'general' are listed under the key 'general' of each scenario and are not repeated under the six needs.
lists.limits: A listed entry may differ from the environment in material, scale, gravity level, flow or fuel; the entry shows what the item states and what it does not. The lists say which statements name the environment's conditions. They do not say what happens in the environment.

sentences.fields: n_at, n_about, n_general: number of entries of the three lists; n_listed: their sum; n_not_full_text: listed entries whose document has an access other than full_text_read; need_phrase: one of 'need_phrase'. {field} is replaced by the field; [field|one|many] chooses the first form when the field is 1 and the second otherwise.

need_phrase.general: as about fire safety in general

sentences.counts_with_ranges: Of the statements quoted from documents of the reference list and tagged {need_phrase}, {n_at} [n_at|states|state] an oxygen concentration and a pressure inside the ranges of this environment; {n_about} more [n_about|states|state] at least one of its conditions (oxygen, pressure or gravity level), as a value inside the range or as a range that overlaps it, and none outside them; {n_general} [n_general|states|state] no oxygen, pressure or gravity level as a value that can be compared.
sentences.counts_without_ranges: This environment sets no oxygen range and no pressure range, so no statement is placed at its oxygen and pressure; of the statements quoted from documents of the reference list and tagged {need_phrase}, {n_about} [n_about|names|name] its gravity level, alone or among several, or partial gravity; {n_general} [n_general|states|state] no oxygen, pressure or gravity level as a value that can be compared.
sentences.nature: These statements are quoted from publications and other documents ({n_not_full_text} of the {n_listed} listed [n_not_full_text|comes|come] from a document that was not read in full text); they are not rows of the PSI tables and were not checked against the raw data.
sentences.none: No statement of the reference list tagged {need_phrase} is listed for this environment.

_meta.forbidden_words_note: findings.py stops if a sentence template or a filled sentence holds one of these words as a whole word. The check covers the sentences of this file only: the quotes of the documents are carried verbatim and some contain such words.

left_out.SAF17S.table1: Says only that a slide reproduces Table I of ICES-2017-224 with identical cells; the cells are carried by SAF17.table1_o2.
left_out.RU16.transducer: A plan written before the flights (future tense) that names an instrument; it reports no observation and no condition of a test.
left_out.ICES15.cstr: An assumption of a dilution model and an input of a calculation (P = 1 atm), not an observation; tagging 1 atm would turn a calculation input into a test condition.
left_out.BASS2SUM.cstr: An assumption of a dilution model; no value and no observation.
left_out.BASS2SUM.idealgas: An input of a calculation (P = 1 atm, T = 300 K), not a reported measurement; tagging 1 atm would turn a calculation input into a test condition.
left_out.PSISAF.o2_traces: Graph readings made by eye by an AI from images in PSI raw-data files; the item's note says they must be replaced by the telemetry numbers before any use as data. Not a statement of a publication.
left_out.PSISAF.pressure_column: Lowest and highest cells of a PSI raw-data column, extracted by the team; it is a reading of raw data, not a statement of a publication, and this layer says of its entries that they were not checked against the raw data.
left_out.PSISAF.pressure_figures: Says that the PSI telemetry documents contain a pressure graph; no value and no observation.
